### Work type

Feature

### Area

Infrastructure

### Priority

Critical

### Objective

Establish a reproducible root pnpm/Turborepo workspace that hosts independently structured `apps/api` and `apps/web` applications, with pragmatic Clean Architecture boundaries and a deliberately narrow sharing model.

### Context

The API and web application are separate delivery units with different responsibilities and external dependencies. They must not mirror folders or layers merely for symmetry. The workspace should make their independent architectures explicit while centralizing only protocol contracts and backend-authoritative business rules where ownership is clear.

### Functional requirements

- Configure the root pnpm workspace and Turborepo task graph.
- Register independently structured `apps/api` and `apps/web` applications.
- Provide `packages/contracts` as the narrow cross-application protocol boundary.
- Provide `packages/domain` as the backend-authoritative home of business rules.
- Support repository-wide install, build, lint, type-check, and test commands.

### Technical requirements

- Define root workspace metadata, package manifests, and Turbo scripts for reproducible orchestration.
- Keep `apps/api` and `apps/web` independently structured; do not require mirrored folders, layers, or abstractions.
- Apply pragmatic Clean Architecture inside each application according to its own responsibilities.
- Limit `packages/contracts` to runtime-validatable DTO, API, and event contracts plus correlation IDs.
- Keep authoritative business rules in `packages/domain`, owned and consumed by the backend; the web application must not import it.
- Do not share backend use cases, repository interfaces, persistence models, or provider SDK types.
- Do not share frontend state models, view models, presentation concerns, or UI-specific orchestration.
- Enforce frozen installation and verifiable import boundaries through workspace scripts and automated checks.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A frozen pnpm install succeeds from the repository root.
- [ ] Turbo can run build, lint, type-check, and test scripts across the workspace.
- [ ] `apps/api` and `apps/web` are independently structured and do not mirror layers by convention.
- [ ] `packages/contracts` exposes only runtime-validatable protocol contracts and correlation IDs.
- [ ] `packages/domain` remains backend-authoritative and is not imported by the web application.
- [ ] Automated checks reject prohibited cross-boundary and provider/framework imports.

### Dependencies

None.

### Testing strategy

Verify frozen installation, workspace graph discovery, Turbo task execution, TypeScript/lint/test foundations, runtime contract validation, and explicit allowed/forbidden import fixtures for both applications.

### Definition of Done

- [ ] Root workspace and package boundaries are reproducible from a clean checkout.
- [ ] Independent API and web architecture constraints are documented and machine-verifiable.
- [ ] Shared contracts and backend domain ownership are explicit.
- [ ] Acceptance and boundary checks pass in CI-compatible commands.

### Work type

Feature

### Area

Infrastructure

### Priority

High

### Objective

Deploy `apps/api` to Railway as a container image built from a repository Dockerfile, together with the deployment artifacts, secret boundaries and the Railway agent tooling (CLI, MCP server, `use-railway` skill) configured at project scope.

### Context

Feature derived from docs/planning/DEMO.md and the implementation sequence.
Parent issue: #10.

The hosting provider decision changed from Fly.io to Railway (Hobby plan). Fly.io was never implemented: docs/architecture/deploy-planning.md §2/§4 prescribed `fly.toml`, `flyctl` and the Fly.io MCP, but no deployment artifact exists in the repository today. That document must be retargeted to Railway as part of this Feature.

The build path is a repository Dockerfile built remotely by Railway, not a zero-config builder. Verified reason: the root package.json declares `engines.node: ">=24.0.0 <25.0.0"` and `engine-strict` is enabled, so `pnpm install` aborts with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE` on any other Node version. Docker's explicit `node:24-alpine` base is deterministic; Railway's default builder (Railpack) resolves Node from `engines.node`/`.nvmrc` and falls back to its own default `22`, which the engines gate rejects.

The planned Dockerfile was validated against the current repository. Its production stage is correct as written; three corrections are required and are listed under Technical requirements.

Scope note: docs/architecture/deploy-planning.md §4 classified the agent tooling (CLI/MCP/skill) as local environment setup outside the demo's functional scope. This Feature now carries it explicitly, so the deployment is reproducible by any contributor rather than only on one machine.

### Functional requirements

- A single container image runs the Fastify API (apps/api) on Railway and answers `GET /health` with `200`.
- The image carries production dependencies only and contains no test fixtures, local env files or repository VCS data.
- Runtime configuration is supplied as service variables; no secret is baked into the image or committed.
- The API binds the port Railway injects and is reachable on a generated Railway domain.
- Deployments are reproducible from a clean checkout, and a failing build is visible in the deploy logs.
- A contributor can reproduce the deployment from documented commands without prior Railway state.

### Technical requirements

- Follow docs/planning/DEMO.md and approved monorepo boundaries.
- Keep provider integrations replaceable and failures sanitised.
- Dockerfile at `apps/api/Dockerfile`, with the build context at the monorepo root: its COPY paths are root-relative (`packages/contracts/...`, `apps/api/...`).
- Base image `node:24-alpine` (mandatory, see Context) with `corepack prepare pnpm@11.27.0 --activate`.
- Build order is load-bearing: `packages/contracts` and `packages/domain` must be built before `apps/api`, because both export from `dist/` and apps/api/tsconfig.build.json declares no TypeScript `references`.
- Corrections required to the planned Dockerfile:
  1. `COPY .npmrc ./` in both stages. The repository `.npmrc` sets `engine-strict=true` and `manage-package-manager-versions=true`; neither stage copies it today, so the image can be built on a Node version that the CI gates reject, silently.
  2. Add a `.dockerignore` at the repository root. Docker honours `.dockerignore`, never `.gitignore`; `apps/web/.next` measures 495 MB on disk and `.env.local` is present in the working tree, so the build context is currently heavy and any future broad COPY would leak secrets.
  3. Verify `corepack enable` on `node:24-alpine` during the first build. corepack is absent from the development machine and Node has been removing it from its distribution; treat as unverified until observed.
- The `deps`-stage comment in the plan ("pnpm validates `--frozen-lockfile` against every workspace member") is inaccurate: an A/B test showed pnpm tolerates a missing workspace member and still reports the lockfile up to date. The COPY is harmless hygiene; the comment should be corrected rather than relied on.
- Railway integration: `RAILWAY_TOKEN` for CI/CD. The Railway MCP server does not accept project tokens - it requires a user identity for billing and audit - so MCP and CI credentials are separate concerns.
- Agent tooling at project scope, not machine scope: Railway CLI (>= 5.44.0 for MCP), the `use-railway` skill, and the Railway MCP entry registered in both opencode.json (`mcp.railway`) and .mcp.json (`mcpServers.railway`). Entry point: `curl -fsSL agents.railway.com | sh`, or `railway setup agent` / `railway mcp install` / `railway skills install` when the CLI is already installed.
- Documentation: retarget docs/architecture/deploy-planning.md from Fly.io to Railway and correct the stale comment on this issue that cites `fly.toml`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `apps/api/Dockerfile` builds from the monorepo root context on `node:24-alpine`, with `packages/contracts` and `packages/domain` built before `apps/api`.
- [ ] The built image starts the API and `GET /health` returns `200` over the Railway domain.
- [ ] `.dockerignore` exists at the repository root and excludes `node_modules`, `.git`, `.next`, `.turbo`, build reports and `.env*`.
- [ ] `.npmrc` is present in both Dockerfile stages, so `engine-strict` and `manage-package-manager-versions` apply during the image build.
- [ ] No secret, seed, PII or local env file is present in the image or the repository.
- [ ] Required service variables are documented, and `APP_ENV` uses `demo` (`production` is out of scope for this demo).
- [ ] Railway CLI, the `use-railway` skill and the Railway MCP entry are configured at project scope and documented so a second contributor reproduces them.
- [ ] docs/architecture/deploy-planning.md no longer prescribes Fly.io.
- [ ] Required evidence and failure behavior are covered.
- [ ] No unsupported production claims or secrets are introduced.

### Dependencies

- Depends on #15 (closed).
- #30 is no longer a prerequisite. Verified rationale: this Feature ships independently deployable artifacts and does not depend on the AI assessment schema (#20) or the distribution feature (#28) that #30 waits on; the previous ordering was sequencing, not a technical need. #20 and #28 remain prerequisites of #30 only.
- The native GitHub dependency relation `blocked_by #30` was removed, so the dependency graph now matches this text. The only remaining native relation is `blocked_by #15`, which is closed.

### Testing strategy

Workflow validation and build checks. Reproduce the image build from a clean checkout, confirm the build-order and engine gates fail loudly when violated, and record the observed `GET /health` response from the deployed service. The evidence Task records actual results and must not claim unexecuted checks.

### Definition of Done

- Feature behavior, tests and evidence are complete.
- Required tests and validation pass, or bounded external limitations are documented.
- No secrets, seeds, PII or unsupported production claims are introduced.

### Work type

Task

### Area

Backend

Critical

### Objective

Implement the smallest backend-authoritative application-review lifecycle and its portable runtime-validatable protocol representation, establishing the first bounded slice of Feature #12 without absorbing downstream AI, persistence, Stellar, or telemetry work.

### Context

- First implementation unit under Feature #12.
- Workspace/application scaffolds and architecture boundaries completed through #37.
- #116 already introduced Zod 4, branded `CorrelationId`, its parser and generator, and Fastify propagation; reuse that foundation rather than duplicating it.
- Replace bootstrap-only probes with the first real domain and protocol exports when no verified consumer still requires them.

### Functional requirements

- Define exactly these domain lifecycle states: `draft`, `awaiting_assessment`, `human_review`, `approved`, `changes_requested`, and `rejected`.
- Allow exactly these transitions:
  - `draft -> awaiting_assessment`
  - `awaiting_assessment -> human_review`
  - `human_review -> approved | changes_requested | rejected`
  - `changes_requested -> draft`
- Treat `approved` and `rejected` as terminal states for this slice.
- Reject every other transition with an explicit domain error and no partial mutation.
- Provide a branded, runtime-validatable opaque UUID v4 `ApplicationId`.
- Provide a runtime-validatable application-review state schema.
- Provide a strict minimal snapshot schema containing only `applicationId` and `state`.
- Keep wire and domain vocabulary compatible without making `packages/domain` depend on `packages/contracts`.

### Technical requirements

- Keep transition rules and invariants in `packages/domain`.
- Keep Zod/runtime protocol validation in `packages/contracts`, reusing the existing Zod 4 catalog dependency.
- Add no runtime dependencies to `packages/domain`.
- Keep `packages/contracts` portable for Node and DOM-only consumers.
- Reject unknown state values, malformed IDs, and unknown snapshot fields.
- Introduce no framework, persistence, provider SDK, UI, or infrastructure types.
- Retire `WorkspaceProbe`, `describeWorkspace`, `isWorkspaceBootstrapped`, and `apiBootstrapProbe` only when their verified consumers have been removed or replaced.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/domain` exports the application-review lifecycle states, transition rules, and invariants.
- [ ] Every allowed transition succeeds: `draft -> awaiting_assessment`, `awaiting_assessment -> human_review`, each `human_review` outcome, and `changes_requested -> draft`.
- [ ] An invalid transition returns an explicit domain error and leaves the prior state unchanged with no partial mutation.
- [ ] `approved` and `rejected` reject every outgoing transition.
- [ ] `packages/contracts` exports branded `ApplicationId`, its runtime parser, the application-review state schema, and the strict minimal snapshot schema.
- [ ] A snapshot with a valid UUID v4 `applicationId` and a valid state parses successfully.
- [ ] Contract validation rejects malformed UUIDs, unknown states, missing required fields, and unknown fields.
- [ ] Wire and domain vocabulary remain compatible without a `packages/domain -> packages/contracts` runtime dependency.

- Define the persistence ownership of identity, account, and session records without allowing browser code or authentication adapters to mutate backend-authoritative domain state.
- Treat any future inclusion in the bounded demo critical path as an explicit scope change rather than an implicit dependency.

### Technical requirements
- Use NextAuth v5 / Auth.js at the server-side Next.js boundary for authentication and web-session lifecycle.
- Document and enforce the boundary map: Auth.js authenticates users and manages web sessions; the backend validates trusted identity and owns authorization; a server-only persistence adapter owns authentication records; domain persistence remains behind backend application ports.
- Reconcile the existing optional Supabase Auth direction as superseded for this scope. Supabase may remain the PostgreSQL platform, but Supabase Auth must not become a parallel identity or session authority.
- Depend on #14 for typed validation of provider credentials, session secrets, callback URLs, and environment-specific configuration. Secrets must remain server-only and must not be read ad hoc from presentation code.

### Work type

Technical/Foundation

### Area

Infrastructure

### Priority

Medium

### Objective

Make the root `tests/` suite subject to the same static analysis as every workspace, so lint and type errors cannot hide in the files that verify the repository's own gates and boundaries.

### Context

This does not come from `docs/planning/DEMO.md`. It is a repository-tooling gap found while closing Feature #14 (issues #44, #45 and #46) and it was already recorded as an accepted limitation in the Feature #15 closing evidence, section 5: "`tests/**` de la raíz no está cubierto por `turbo run lint`". This issue tracks fixing it rather than continuing to carry it.

The gate itself came from Feature #15. `pnpm run verify` runs `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run typecheck`, and both are `turbo run <task>`, which only walks pnpm workspaces: `apps/*` and `packages/*`. The root `tests/` directory is not a workspace, so it is never linted or typechecked by any gate, even though `pnpm run test:boundaries` executes its test files on every pull request.

### Functional requirements

Technical-only: no user-visible behavior changes. The observable difference is that `pnpm run verify` fails on a lint or type error introduced in a root test file, instead of passing because nothing looked at it.

### Technical requirements

Measured on `main` at `c8adefe`:

- There is **no root `tsconfig.json`** — only `tsconfig.base.json`, which is an `extends` target and has no `include`. So there is no project for the root test files to be typechecked against.
- `turbo run lint` and `turbo run typecheck` declare no root-level inputs; they dispatch to the workspaces only.
- There are **26 `.ts` files under `tests/`**: 4 test files (`boundaries.test.ts`, `testing-and-ci-gates.test.ts`, `application-review-round-trip.test.ts`, `config-secret-boundaries.test.ts`) plus 22 fixtures and provider stubs.

**The constraint that makes this non-trivial.** `tests/fixtures/boundaries/**` deliberately contains code that violates the rules it verifies: for example `tests/fixtures/boundaries/apps/api/src/application/imports-fastify.fixture.ts` is literally `import Fastify from "fastify"`, and provider stubs sit under fake `node_modules` directories. Those modules resolve only inside their workspaces, not from the repository root. A new configuration must therefore include the test sources **and** exclude `tests/fixtures/boundaries/**`, or it will both fail typecheck and contradict the invariant asserted by the test "fixture paths stay under `tests/fixtures/boundaries/`, so no real `apps/*/src` or `packages/*/src` include (used by build, lint, and typecheck) ever matches them". Note that one fixture group already carries its own `tsconfig.json` (`tests/fixtures/boundaries/apps/web/`) precisely because a test compiles it on purpose.

Verification that the gap is latent rather than currently hiding defects: `npx eslint tests/` lints 23 files and reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. The problem is that nothing invokes it, not that violations exist today.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A root-level typecheck covers the 4 test files under `tests/` and fails on a type error introduced in any of them.
- [ ] A root-level lint covers the test files under `tests/` and fails on a lint error introduced in any of them.
- [ ] `tests/fixtures/boundaries/**` stays excluded from both, so the invariant asserted in `tests/boundaries.test.ts` keeps holding and the self-violating fixtures are not "fixed".
- [ ] `pnpm run verify` runs both, so the coverage is enforced in CI and not only available as a manual command.
- [ ] `pnpm run verify` still exits 0 on an unmodified working tree.
- [ ] The change adds no dependency that is not already present in the repository.

### Dependencies

None. Independent of the demo sequence. Related background only: Feature #15 (issues #47, #48, #49) introduced the gate and recorded the limitation this issue resolves.

### Testing strategy

RED: introduce one type error and one lint error in turn inside a root test file and confirm the new gate catches each. Also confirm the fixtures still do not break the configuration — the negative case matters more than the positive one here, because the fixtures are invalid by design.

GREEN: the same two probes fail the gate, and `pnpm run verify` exits 0 with the probes removed.

REFACTOR: keep the configuration declarative and small; do not restructure the existing test files to satisfy it.

Test level: gate meta-test. Whether the new coverage is itself asserted by `tests/testing-and-ci-gates.test.ts` (which already asserts the workflow, Playwright config and documented commands) is a decision for the implementation.

### Definition of Done

`pnpm run verify` enforces lint and typecheck over the root test files and exits 0 on a clean tree; the fixture-exclusion invariant still holds and is proven, not assumed; the two probes above were run and their results recorded; and the accepted limitation is removed from the standing-limitations list of the Feature #15 evidence document, or explicitly re-stated if it is only partially resolved.

### Work type
Technical/Foundation

### Area
Security / Database

### Priority
High

### Objective
Create the RLS policies — or record the deliberate decision not to — for `public.application_review` and `public.human_decision`, two tables that today have RLS enabled with zero policies.

### Context

This issue exists because a follow-up was **orphaned**. The closing evidence for Feature [#13](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/13) defers the end-user RLS policies to [#134](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/134) — it says so twice, in §5 (límite 2) and §9. **That pointer is wrong.** #134 is "Establish Auth.js authentication and session boundaries": nothing to do with RLS, and closed with its own criteria unmarked. A search across every issue, open and closed, for "RLS" returns nothing. No issue tracked this work until this one.

It also understated the scope. The evidence names only `application_review`; `human_decision` has the same shape, and it arrived later from a **different** Feature ([#19](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/19)) — so the pattern was repeated, not inherited.

### Current state, verified live

Queried against the hosted project on **2026-09-20** (`pg_class`, `pg_policies`, and the Supabase security advisor), not read from the migration files:

| Table | RLS enabled | Policies | Table ACL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `application_review` | yes | **0** | `postgres`, `service_role` only |
| `human_decision` | yes | **0** | `postgres`, `service_role` only |

Supabase security advisor: `rls_enabled_no_policy`, level **INFO**, **count 2**.

**Nothing is exposed today.** `anon` and `authenticated` hold no grant at all on either table — `revoke all on public.<table> from anon, authenticated` removed them, and `service_role` is the only application role with access. Postgres answers `42501` (`permission denied`) at the GRANT layer, before RLS is ever evaluated. The API connects as `service_role` and is the only writer.

**The real risk is conditional, and it is worth stating precisely:** the moment any role other than `service_role` or `postgres` receives a GRANT on either table, it gets **unrestricted row-level access to every row**, because there is no policy to filter anything. The absence is currently safe only because the grants are absent. That is a fragile equilibrium — it is one `grant` statement away from a full table read.

### What is blocked, and why

**This cannot be implemented correctly yet, and that is the actual finding — not a lack of time.**

An RLS policy needs a *subject*. `auth.uid()`, a JWT claim, a role — something to write `using (...)` against. This demo has **no authenticated identity whatsoever**: there is no Auth.js, no session, no `auth.uid()`. The only caller is the API acting as `service_role`, which bypasses RLS entirely.

Writing a policy now would mean inventing a security model with no identity to key it on. A policy that returns `true` for everyone would be worse than the documented absence: it would convert an INFO advisory into a real hole while looking fixed.

So the decision that unblocks this is a scope decision, and it has two genuinely different endings:

1. **The demo will never expose these tables to a non-`service_role` caller.** Then the correct resolution is *not* a policy — it is an explicit, recorded decision plus a guard so the equilibrium cannot drift silently (an assertion that no grant ever reaches a non-service role, and the advisor's INFO acknowledged as accepted). Cheap, honest, and closes the loop.
2. **End-user access is coming** (which is what #134 would bring). Then the policies must express the identity→row relationship — e.g. an SME reading only its own `application_review` — and that mapping does not exist yet. The policies become a Task under whatever Feature introduces the identity, with this issue as the prerequisite record.

**Recommendation: resolve it as 1 now and re-open the question when an identity model is actually chosen.** The demo is not exposed, the advisory is INFO, and guessing a policy would be the one move that makes things worse.

### What is out of an agent's reach

Everything below is either yours to decide or needs your explicit go-ahead. Nothing else blocks this.

- **The identity model.** Only you can decide whether any non-`service_role` caller will ever read these tables, and under what rule. Without that, any policy I write is a guess. *(Decided by you — genuinely out of an agent's reach.)*
- **Applying a migration to the hosted project.** I can author `supabase/migrations/*.sql`, and the Supabase MCP is connected — I used it to read the state above, so I can apply DDL. But this is a **shared live project**, so applying it is your call, not my default. *(I am able, needs your go-ahead.)*
- **Whether `service_role` remains the only access path.** An architecture decision that is yours. *(Decided by you.)*

If the answer is 1, there may be **no migration at all** — just a recorded decision and a guard test. Those I can write.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The RLS gap is resolved by an explicit decision recorded in the repository: either policies that express a defined identity rule, or a documented decision that `service_role` is the only access path for the bounded demo.
- [ ] `application_review` and `human_decision` are both covered — the evidence that named only one table is not the scope.
- [ ] If the decision is "no policies", a guard exists so that a future GRANT to a non-`service_role` role cannot land silently.
- [ ] The Supabase security advisor's `rls_enabled_no_policy` finding is either resolved or explicitly acknowledged as accepted, with its level named.
- [ ] Feature [#13](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/13)'s evidence no longer points at [#134](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/134) for this work.

### Dependencies
- Depends on an identity/scope decision (see above). Not blocked by code.
- Related: [#134](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/134) (Auth.js boundaries) is where an end-user identity would come from, if one ever does.

### Testing strategy
If a guard is the resolution: a deterministic test asserting that neither table grants anything to `anon` or `authenticated`, derived from the migration files rather than a hand-maintained list, and asserted to find the revocations so it cannot pass vacuously. If policies are the resolution: an integration test against the live project proving a non-`service_role` caller sees only its own rows.

### Definition of Done
The decision is recorded, both tables are covered, and either the policies or the guard are in place with the advisor finding acknowledged. No unsupported production claim about authentication is introduced — this repository has no auth layer today and the issue must not imply one.

### Objective
Custody the campaign funding in a Stellar contract so that the goal condition is enforced by the ledger: atomic payout to the SME when the goal is reached, and permissionless refunds to investors when the deadline passes without it.

### Context
Epic derived from the demo plan. It replaces the decision recorded on 2026-09-14 that contracts were optional extension work, never required or blocking.

Today the funding is a classic direct payment, verified from a signed XDR. That leaves custody of the funds to the SME's good faith plus an off-chain calculation: nothing at protocol level prevents the SME from keeping the contribution. Stellar Claimable Balance (CAP-23) was evaluated as a contract-free alternative and **rejected** — its claim predicates have time-only leaves, so "the goal was reached" is not expressible on-chain. ### Work type
Feature

### Area
Stellar

### Priority
Critical

### Objective
Implement the factory and the campaign vault contract: one vault per campaign, with custody of the contributions, atomic payout when the goal is reached, voluntary withdrawal before the goal, and permissionless refunds with a bounded sweep.

### Context
Feature derived from `docs/planning/stellar-blockchain-requirements.md`, section "Detalle técnico: custodia por contrato de campaña".
Parent issue: #235.

This is the funding path of the demo. It supersedes the classic direct payment as the way money moves in, which is why #24's XDR engine stops being the funding path (see the sibling Feature on persistence). The state machine, function surface and factory pattern are already agreed and documented; this Feature implements them.

### Functional requirements
- A factory that deploys one campaign vault per campaign, holding no funds itself.
- A campaign vault with `__constructor(sme, token, goal, deadline)` that fixes the destination, asset, goal and deadline once and cannot re-run.
- `contribute(investor, amount)` authenticated by the investor, allowed only while the state is `Funding` and before the deadline. It adds to the total and, when the total reaches the goal, moves to `Settled` and transfers to the SME **in the same transaction**.
- `withdraw(investor)` authenticated by the investor, allowed only while `Funding`, returning the contribution to the registered address.
- `refund(investor)` permissionless, allowed only in `Refunding`, paying the registered address.
- `sweep(investors)` permissionless, allowed only in `Refunding`, with a bounded batch size.
- Read functions for state, total, goal, deadline, SME and contribution of an investor.
- An index of contributors so the sweep can enumerate them.
- One event per deployment and events for auditable state changes.
- The state transition is decided **inside** `contribute`, so ledger ordering makes it deterministic against a concurrent withdrawal.

### Technical requirements
- Rust plus `soroban-sdk` major 28. `#![no_std]`, target `wasm32v1-none`.
- Use `__constructor`, never a guarded `initialize`, so reinitialization is impossible.
- `Address::require_auth()` on the investor for `contribute` and `withdraw`; none for reads.
- Bounded loops: never iterate an attacker-shaped list without a cap.
- Keep factory logic separate from vault logic.
- Extend TTLs proactively and treat the deadline as data, never as a TTL: the TTL is not a security mechanism.
- Value-bearing contract, so the security checklist applies in full: events for state changes, no unbounded footprints, and an explicit decision on upgradeability and pause controls.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reaching the goal pays the SME in the same transaction that crosses the threshold
- [ ] Contributing after the goal is reached reverts
- [ ] Withdrawing before the goal returns the contribution
- [ ] After the deadline without the goal, refund and sweep return contributions to the registered address
- [ ] Sweeping does not rescue funds to anyone but the registered contributor
- [ ] `__constructor` cannot run twice
- [ ] The contract address is deterministic per `(deployer, salt)` and computable without deploying
- [ ] The contract is deployed on Testnet and its address is verifiable in the explorer

### Dependencies
- Depends on the toolchain Feature of #235
- Supersedes the funding path of #24 (closed; not reopened)

### Testing strategy
Unit tests with the SDK test environment, covering the goal-reached path, the deadline-expired path, authorization, TTL and events. Negative tests for double claim, contributions after settlement, refunds before the deadline and out-of-batch sweep. A local-network integration test. See `docs/planning/stellar-blockchain-requirements.md`, Part 3, section 2.

### Definition of Done
- Feature behavior, tests and evidence are complete.
- Required tests and validation pass, or bounded external limitations are documented.
- No secrets, seeds, PII or unsupported production claims are introduced.

### Work type
Task

### Area
Stellar

### Priority
Critical

### Objective
Write the factory and the campaign vault contract in Rust, implementing the agreed state machine and function surface.

### Context
Task derived from Feature #236.
Parent issue: #236.

The state machine, the function surface and the factory pattern are already agreed and documented in `docs/planning/stellar-blockchain-requirements.md`. This Task implements them; it does not re-decide them. Design decisions and advisories: `odd/tasks/soroban-campaign-vault-decision.md`.

### Functional requirements
- Factory with `deploy(owner, wasm_hash, salt, constructor_args) -> Address`, authorized by the owner, holding no funds, emitting one event per deployment.
- Vault with `__constructor(sme, token, goal, deadline)`, running once and never again.
- `contribute(investor, amount)`: investor auth, only in `Funding` and before the deadline; adds to the total and, on reaching the goal, moves to `Settled` and transfers to the SME **in the same transaction**.
- `withdraw(investor)`: investor auth, only in `Funding`, returns the contribution to the registered address.
- `refund(investor)`: permissionless, only in `Refunding`, pays the registered address.
- `sweep(investors)`: permissionless, only in `Refunding`, bounded batch.
- A contributor index so the sweep can enumerate.
- Read functions for state, total, goal, deadline, SME and an investor's contribution.
- Events for auditable state changes.

### Technical requirements
- Rust, `#![no_std]`, target `wasm32v1-none`, `soroban-sdk` major 28.
- The goal check lives **inside** `contribute`, so ledger ordering makes it deterministic against a concurrent withdrawal.
- Typed `#[contracttype]` storage keys; persistent storage for per-investor data, instance storage for globals within the 64KB cap.
- Extend TTLs proactively. The deadline is data compared against the ledger time, never a TTL.
- Bounded loops only: never iterate an unbounded, attacker-shaped list.
- Keep factory logic separate from vault logic.
- Value-bearing contract: the security checklist applies in full. Decide and document upgradeability and pause explicitly.
- Never renumber error codes after release.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reaching the goal pays the SME in the same transaction that crosses the threshold
- [ ] Contributing after settlement reverts
- [ ] Withdrawing before the goal returns the contribution
- [ ] After the deadline without the goal, refund and sweep pay the registered address

But custody during a campaign is now the contract's, not the person's, and the honest limits are stronger than the demo previously had to state. Leaving the old copy in place would make the demo claim more than it proves.

### Functional requirements
- State that contributions are held by the contract during the campaign, and that this is code custody: no person holds a key to those funds.
- State that the contract cannot be made to pay anyone but the fixed destination, and that the destination is immutable once the vault exists.
- State the honest limits: no recovery mechanism and no clawback, so funds no one claims can only leave through the sweep and may otherwise stay in the contract.
- State that the goal condition is enforced by the contract, and that the deadline refund requires a transaction to be sent — permissionless, but not self-firing.
- Keep the existing disclosures that remain true: Testnet and no real value, non-custodial signing, AI under human supervision, not fit for production.
- Update `docs/design/demo-ui.md` and the disclosure blocks in `docs/planning/DEMO.md` together, so they cannot drift.

### Technical requirements
- Copy in Spanish, consistent with the existing UI copy.
- Follow the established disclosure format and the simulation-labelling convention.
- Introduce no claim about legality, custody, profitability or provider quality.
- Do not describe the contract as audited or as production-ready.
- Keep the AI disclosure intact: the AI does not approve, sign, calculate obligations or move funds.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every disclosure that described a direct payment is reconciled with contract custody
- [ ] The custody-during-campaign nuance is stated explicitly, not left implied
- [ ] The no-recovery and no-clawback limits are stated
- [ ] The permissionless-but-not-self-firing nature of the refund is stated
- [ ] No disclosure claims a guarantee the contract does not provide
- [ ] The two documents are updated together and do not contradict each other

### Dependencies

- Relates to #17 (trust disclosures and synthetic fixtures, closed)

### Testing strategy
The sibling Task of this Feature covers the rendering assertions and the claim-by-claim review.

### Definition of Done

- Required tests and validation pass, or bounded external limitations are documented.
- No secrets, seeds, PII or unsupported production claims are introduced.

### Work type
Task

API

High

### Objective
Enable CORS on the Fastify API so the web app, served from a different origin, can call it from the browser.

### Context
Web client components (`"use client"`) call the API with `fetch` from the browser. With the web on `:3001` and the API on `:3000` (docker and cloud profiles, #271) — and on Vercel vs Railway for the demo — the origins differ, and the API sends no `Access-Control-*` headers: an `OPTIONS` preflight returns 404. The browser therefore blocks every web → API call.

### Functional requirements
- `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (optional) lists exact allowed origins, comma-separated; wildcards and paths are rejected by the typed configuration.
- When it is absent, `APP_ENV=local` allows `http://localhost:3001` and `http://127.0.0.1:3001`; every other environment allows no cross-origin caller.
- Preflight requests from an allowed origin succeed with the matching `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`; requests from any other origin receive no CORS headers.
- `x-correlation-id` remains readable by the browser.

### Acceptance criteria
- Parser and HTTP tests cover allowed, disallowed and unset cases (deterministic, no network).
- `pnpm run verify` stays green.
- The docker profile web (`:3001`) can call the API container (`:3000`) from the browser.
- Docs describe the variable per profile.

### Work type

Technical/Foundation

### Area

Infrastructure / Deployment

### Priority

High

> **Decision recorded (2026-09-24):** the demo is presented with **everything deployed in the cloud**. This issue therefore stays **High**, not Medium — the hosted URL is the delivery surface, not a fallback.

### Objective

Make the hosted frontend surface (`vaqcrow-web` on Vercel) serve the current `main` build with its backend configured, so the demo URL is a live, reproducible deployment instead of a build frozen on 2026-09-19 pointing at a branch that no longer exists.

### Context

This does not come from `docs/planning/DEMO.md`. It is an operational gap found on **2026-09-24** while auditing the project board, and it was never tracked: a search across every issue, open and closed, for "Vercel" returns only [#56](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/56), [#271](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/271) and [#272](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/272) — all closed.

**It is out of Feature [#32](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/32)'s documented boundary, and that is the actual gap.** #32's Objective is *"Deploy `apps/api` to Railway as a container image built from a repository Dockerfile..."*, and all ten of its acceptance criteria are API/Railway: `apps/api/Dockerfile`, `GET /health` over the Railway domain, root `.dockerignore`, `.npmrc` in both stages, service variables, the Railway CLI/MCP/skill, and retargeting `deploy-planning.md` away from Fly.io. **None mentions Vercel, the production branch, a custom domain, the web base URL, or `vercel.json`.** The repository already says so itself: `docs/architecture/deploy-planning.md` §Fase 1 records *"#101 — API entregada: desplegada y verificada en Railway. Restan la web (Vercel) y los workflows."* The web half was orphaned.

This is a defect, not environment preparation, which is why it is filed separately rather than folded into #32: #32 carries CI workflows, preview validation and promotion/rollback policy, and an operational outage should not travel hidden inside it.

### Current state, verified live

Read from the Vercel API for project `vaqcrow-web` (team `reyduars-projects`) and from the repository on **2026-09-24**, not inferred from documentation:

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| The `release` branch **does not exist** | `git ls-remote --heads origin` returns only `main` plus task branches; no local `release` either |
| Production is **frozen since 2026-09-19 12:03** | Newest production-target deployment is `dpl_EQYALRRB58SgX4mdpuzkbvXsHdZS`, `githubCommitRef: "release"`, sha `f044f2c` |
| The 8 production deployments before it came from `main` (Sep 18–19); every deployment after it is **preview only** | 15 most recent deployments all carry `target: null` |
| Vercel reports the project as **not live** | `get_project` → `live: false` |
| **Zero environment variables** | `filter_project_envs` → `envs: []`, `hiddenProductionEnvCount: 0` |
| The deployed web therefore has **no backend** | `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` is unset, and `createAssessmentGateway` / `createFundingIntentGateway` return `null` when the URL is empty; the UI renders *"No hay backend configurado, así que no se puede consultar una evaluación real."* |
| The deployment is **not reproducible from a checkout** | No `vercel.json` and no `.vercel/project.json` in the repository, although `deploy-planning.md` §3 documents both |
| **The documented variable name is wrong** | `apps/web/src` reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`, but `deploy-planning.md` prescribes `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` — in the `vercel.json` example (line 325), the configuration table (line 350) and the CLI commands (lines 1128 and 1131). Following the document configures a variable nothing reads, which reproduces the "no backend" state exactly |
| A **zombie domain** remains from the deleted branch | `vaqcrow-web-git-release-reyduars-projects.vercel.app` |
| Vercel Authentication covers **previews only** | `ssoProtection.deploymentType: "all_except_custom_domains"` |

**Verified working, so it is not part of this issue:** the production domain `vaqcrow-web-nine.vercel.app` is reachable **without a Vercel account** (confirmed with an anonymous request, not an authenticated one), the API at `api-production-c07f.up.railway.app` answers `GET /health` with `200`, and its CORS preflight from the deployed web origin returns `204` with the correct `access-control-allow-origin`. The frontend and backend are correctly wired; only the frontend's configuration is missing.

**Also observed:** the `/request` step renders a visible English placeholder block — *"Step content coming soon — This step is a placeholder. Content will be implemented in a future update."* It appears in production **and** in the latest `main` preview, so redeploying does not remove it.

### What is out of an agent's reach

Everything below is either yours to decide or needs your explicit go-ahead. This is the complete list; nothing else blocks the issue.

- **Changing the production branch in the Vercel dashboard.** The Vercel MCP is connected and I can read the project, but the production branch is a project setting, not repository state. *(Needs your go-ahead — I can drive it through the API if you authorise it, or you change it in Settings → Git.)*
- **Setting `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` for Production and Preview.** Same reasoning. It is a public variable and carries no secret. *(Needs your go-ahead.)*
- **Adopting a custom domain.** A purchase and a naming decision. *(Decided by you.)*
- **Whether previews should stay behind Vercel Authentication.** Today they are. Leaving them protected is defensible; sharing a preview link with the tribunal is then impossible. *(Decided by you.)*

The repository side — `vercel.json`, the `.env.*.example` entries, and reconciling `deploy-planning.md` §3 with the file that actually exists and the name the code actually reads — I can author.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A production deployment exists whose commit matches the current `main` HEAD, and the production branch is either `main` or a branch that is actually maintained — no production configuration pointing at a branch that does not exist.
- [ ] `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` is set for Production and Preview, pointing at the Railway API, and verified by a real request from the deployed origin rather than by reading the setting back.
- [ ] `vercel.json` is committed at the repository root with the configuration `deploy-planning.md` §3 already prescribes (build command, `outputDirectory: apps/web/.next`, region, framework), and the document and the file agree.
- [ ] Every occurrence of the web base URL in `deploy-planning.md` names the variable the code actually reads, including the CLI commands, so following the document cannot reproduce the current broken state.
- [ ] The web base URL is documented where a contributor will look for it, not only in the dashboard.
- [ ] The stale `vaqcrow-web-git-release-*` domain is removed.
- [ ] No placeholder block is visible anywhere on the demo journey surface.
- [ ] The decision on Vercel Authentication for previews is recorded, and the URL shared with the tribunal is reachable without a Vercel account.
- [ ] The custom-domain decision is recorded, whether adopted or explicitly deferred.
- [ ] No secret, seed or PII is committed, and no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable carries a secret value.

### Dependencies

- Not blocked by code, and not blocked by [#30](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/30): the configuration is independent of what the journey eventually renders.
- **Related and jointly required for the cloud demo:** [#287](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/287) — the hosted API's campaign-vault configuration. The frontend being configured is not sufficient; the vault routes are currently not registered on the hosted API at all.
- Related: [#32](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/32) owns the Railway/API side and the CI workflows; this issue deliberately does not.
- Related: [#240](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/240) — the deployed surface still shows the pre-contract-custody trust disclosures, so a redeploy landing before #240 closes will publish stale disclosure copy.
- Related: [#271](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/271) and [#272](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/272), which produced the environment profiles and CORS the deployed web depends on.

### Testing strategy

Verify by observation against the live deployment rather than by configuration readback: an unauthenticated request to the production URL returns `200`; the served commit equals `main` HEAD; the application reaches the API from the deployed origin (CORS preflight plus one real call); and the rendered journey contains no placeholder text. Record the served commit and the observed results, and state plainly any criterion that could not be verified.

### Definition of Done

Production serves the current `main` build with its backend configured and reachable, the repository carries the deployment configuration instead of only the dashboard, the documented variable name matches the code, both open decisions are recorded, and the zombie domain is gone. No unsupported production claim is introduced — this is a demo deployment on Testnet and the issue must not imply otherwise.

### Work type

Technical/Foundation

### Area

Infrastructure / Backend

### Priority

High

### Objective

Enable the campaign-vault configuration on the hosted API, so the mandatory custody path — the one `DEMO.md` lists as never cut — actually runs in the demo environment instead of being silently absent.

### Context

Found on **2026-09-24** while verifying what "the whole demo deployed in the cloud" requires. It was never tracked: the keys were noted as *"Pendiente del usuario"* inside `odd/tasks/campaign-vault-web-journey.md`, which is working-notes state, not a tracked issue.

Feature [#32](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/32) nominally owns the API's service variables, but its Objective is the Docker image and the Railway agent tooling, and its variable criterion predates this work — so the gap has no owner. This issue is the environment prerequisite for [#237](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/237) / [#247](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/247).

### Current state, verified live

The hosted API was read through the Railway API on **2026-09-24**: project `vaqcrow-api`, service `api`, environment `production`, source `reyduar/Vaqcrow@main`, region `us-west2`, latest deployment `SUCCESS`. Variable **names** only — the connected app cannot read values, which is the correct boundary here.

| Present | Absent |
|---|---|
| `APP_ENV`, `PORT`, `LOG_LEVEL` | `STELLAR_CAMPAIGN_FACTORY_ID` |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | `STELLAR_PLATFORM_SECRET_KEY` |
| `LLM_PROVIDER`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY` | `STELLAR_TOKEN_CONTRACT_ID` *(optional)* |
| `STELLAR_NETWORK` | `STELLAR_RPC_URL` *(optional)* |
| `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` *(sealed)* | |
| nine `RAILWAY_*` system variables | |

**The consequence is not a misconfiguration — it is a missing route surface.** `apps/api/src/application/config/campaign-vault-config.ts` resolves the vault this way:

```ts
if (!hasFactory && !hasSecret) {
  return { ok: true, value: Object.freeze({ enabled: false }) };   // ← the cloud state
}
if (hasFactory !== hasSecret) { /* hard ConfigurationError: "required together" */ }
```

With neither key present the vault resolves to `enabled: false`, and `build-app.ts` registers the campaign routes only when `dependencies.campaign` exists. So on the hosted API **`/campaigns` is not registered at all**: a browser hitting the vault journey from the deployed web gets a `404`, not a partial or degraded response.

`docs/architecture/deploy-planning.md` and `.env.cloud.example` do not contain these keys either, so the documented cloud profile cannot produce a working vault even if followed literally.

**Not required, for the record:** `STELLAR_RPC_URL` falls back to the built-in Testnet constant when `STELLAR_NETWORK=testnet`, and `tokenContractId` is derived by infrastructure when absent. Only the two keys above gate the vault.

### What is out of an agent's reach

- **The platform secret's value.** I will never invent, generate or guess it. It must come from you, and it must be the key that already signs `factory.deploy()` for the deployed factory — a fresh key would not match the contract already on Testnet. *(Yours to supply.)*
- **Writing a signing secret into the hosted environment.** Setting a secret is not the same as setting a public variable, and it is your call even though the Railway MCP is connected. *(Needs your explicit go-ahead.)*
- **Whether the platform secret should live in Railway at all**, versus a managed secret store. Today it would sit as a service variable readable by anyone who can read the service. For a demo on Testnet that may be acceptable, but it is a decision to record, not to assume. *(Decided by you.)*
- **Rotation.** Who replaces the key, and how the factory is re-pointed if it is. *(Decided by you.)*

The repository side — `.env.cloud.example`, the deployment document, and the recorded decision — I can author.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `STELLAR_CAMPAIGN_FACTORY_ID` and `STELLAR_PLATFORM_SECRET_KEY` are set on the hosted API service, matching the factory already deployed on Testnet.
- [ ] The campaign routes are registered on the hosted API, verified by an **observed request** from the deployed web origin rather than by reading the variable list back.
- [ ] `.env.cloud.example` documents the vault keys as placeholders, so the cloud profile is complete and reproducible by a contributor.
- [ ] The platform secret never appears in the repository, this issue, a build log, a deploy log or a serialised response — only the key names and their shapes are recorded.
- [ ] The hosted environment cannot silently enter the half-configured state (one key without the other); the code already fails loudly on that, and the hosted state is confirmed not to be in it.
- [ ] The decision on where the platform secret is stored, and how it is rotated, is recorded alongside the existing secret-boundary work.

### Dependencies

- Related: [#286](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/286) — the frontend surface. Both must close before the cloud demo works end to end.
- Related: [#237](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/237) and [#247](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/247) — this is the environment prerequisite for the vault journey to function.
- Related: [#32](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/32) owns Railway deployment and service-variable documentation.
- Related: [#14](https://github.com/reyduar/Vaqcrow/issues/14) for the platform secret's handling.
- Not blocked by code.

### Testing strategy

Verify against the live deployment: an observed request to the campaign routes from the deployed web origin answers instead of returning `404`, and the vault reports enabled. Confirm the hosted service is not in the half-configured state. Never record the secret's value, and state plainly any criterion that could not be verified.

### Definition of Done

The hosted API serves the campaign-vault routes with the vault enabled against the Testnet factory, the cloud profile documents the keys, the platform secret's storage and rotation are recorded, and no secret value is committed or logged. No unsupported production claim is introduced — this is a Testnet demo, not a custodial production service.
